title: French Revolutionary Decimal Clock
intro: This clock represents a local civil day on a decimal scale, rather than the conventional 24-hour clock. It is a time display, not a change to the underlying timestamp.
structure: Each day has ten decimal hours, each hour has 100 decimal minutes, and each minute has 100 decimal seconds. The reading rolls from 9:99:99 to 0:00:00 at local midnight.
example: Local midnight is 0:00:00, conventional noon is 5:00:00, and 18:00 is 7:50:00. When seconds are hidden, 7:50 is the same reading at decimal-minute resolution.
history: The notation follows French Revolutionary decimal-time arithmetic. It is distinct from the French Republican date calendar and can be selected independently of that calendar.
model: The provider obtains local microseconds of day from Common. It scales the integer day phase by 100000 ticks per 86400000000 microseconds, flooring the displayed tick. Without seconds it uses 1000 ticks per day. The next visible tick is scheduled at the following boundary, rounded upward to a millisecond.
limits: This implementation uses the supplied civil offset, not historical Paris mean time. It does not require geographic coordinates; it is not a reconstruction of historical local timekeeping or a separate astronomical day.
